provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. Term by term the two agree, with the Lean asserting more in two places. (a) Derivatives: the paper bounds one mixed Cartesian partial ∂_x^α ∂_t^b at a time; the Lean bounds the operator norm of the full m-th iterated Fréchet derivative. Since the coordinate directions of SpaceTime = ℝ × Space are unit vectors, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ m f w‖ dominates |∂_x^α ∂_t^b f(w)| for every α, b with |α| + b = m, so the Lean clause gives the paper's for each m = |α| + b. (b) Exponent: the paper quantifies over integers N; the Lean quantifies over every real r ≥ 0 (the power is rpow), which includes the integers. The remaining items match: C depends on (m, r, X) only, exactly the paper's C_{α,b,N,X₁}; 'q ↓ 0' is the Lean's ∃ δ > 0 with the bound for all q < δ; '0 ≤ X ≤ X₁' is `radialEnergy w.2 / physicalQ h w ≤ X`, the lower bound being automatic because radialEnergy ≥ 0. In the converse direction the paper's bound returns the Lean's only up to a dimensional constant, so the two are equivalent up to constants and the Lean side is the stronger literal statement.
